newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Merrill to advise Koor, Clal on cement holdings.
newsitem.headline: Merrill to advise Koor, Clal on cement holdings.

text.p: Koor Industries Ltd and Clal Israel Ltd have chosen Merrill Lynch to act as adviser in the sale of part of their joint cement holdings, a Koor spokesman said on Monday.
Koor and Clal each own 50 percent of Mashav Initiating & Development Ltd, which in turn owns 100 percent of Nesher Israel Cement Enterprises, Israel's cement monopoly.

Mashav president Joseph Rosen and chairman Benjamin Gaon selected Merrill Lynch to evaluate the worth of the cement company. The investment firm will also have to recommend whether Koor and Clal should seek a financial or strategic partner for Nesher or whether the parent company Mashav should go public either in Israel or in the United States.
Rosen said Merrill Lynch must make its recommendation by the end of this year. Koor and Clal will then evaluate the recommendation and reach a position.

Gaon, who is also president and chief executive of Koor, announced last year that the major shareholders had started talks with three leading international cement manufacturers about the possibility of becoming strategic partners in Nesher.
Gaon and his spokesman would not disclose further details on these negotiations.

But last month a Koor source said the company was negotiating with four companies for the sale of a 20 percent stake in Nesher. Talks were underway with France's Lafarge, Mexico's Cemex, Italy's Italcementi and Switzerland's Holderbank, said the source, who asked not to be identified.
Nesher has been seeking a partner as a means of breaking into the Middle East market.
Nesher's sales suffered in 1996 after Israel closed off the Palestinian West Bank and Gaza Strip out of security concerns. There was also a decline in housing starts in Israel.
